newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET STILL FLUSH, RATES MIXED.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET STILL FLUSH, RATES MIXED.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market continued in surplus on Thursday and short-term trading rates were quoted stable to softer in quiet trade, dealers said.

"The market opened in surplus today...in fact it's going to be in surplus for the whole of September because we have a lot of maturities coming up and that's going to depress the rates," commented a dealer.

On Thursday, discount houses were buying central bank paper at 22.64 percent, the rate set at last Thursday's weekly auction, but were selling them easier at 22 percent from 22.50 percent on the open market.

NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold unchanged at 23.5 and 22.5 percent respectively while bankers acceptance bills were quoted at 22.75 amd 22.25 percent across the board from Wednesday's 22.75 and 22.5 percent.
Call money shed two percent to 20 in a market which opened in surplus of Z551 million from Z$846 million the previous day.
